title: India Summons Meta Executives After Facebook Briefly Blocks PM Modi's Video
excerpt: The IT ministry called Meta's global head of public policy to explain why the prime minister's selfie video was restricted on Facebook, as the government rejected the company's 'automated glitch' explanation.
body:
• Facebook briefly restricted PM Modi's July 23 selfie video addressed to India's youth, then restored it after Meta admitted the removal was "in error"
  • India's IT ministry summoned Meta's global head of public policy, saying the company's explanation was "not reasonable"
  • The incident is the latest in a string of regulatory confrontations between New Delhi and Meta over platform accountability
  • Hyderabad police have separately filed a case against Meta India head Arun Srinivas over anti-Modi content on Facebook

India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology has summoned Meta's global head of public policy after Facebook briefly restricted a video posted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, escalating a confrontation between the world's largest democracy and one of its most-used social media platforms.

The video — a two-minute, 56-second selfie clip posted on July 23 — was Modi's first direct address to Gen Z during a 36-day wave of student protests over leaked examination papers. In it, the prime minister promised stricter laws against paper leaks and said a draft bill would go before the Union Cabinet the following day.

The video had garnered millions of views on Instagram and Facebook before access was suddenly restricted on Facebook in the early hours of July 28. Users saw a notice stating the content had been blocked following a "legal request," according to multiple Indian media reports.

Meta Calls It An Error

"The content was removed in error and has since been restored," a Meta spokesperson said in a statement, attributing the takedown to a glitch in the company's automated content filters.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=ShlDhLRFC-4

The Indian government was not persuaded. Sources told PTI that Meta's explanation was "not reasonable" and that deeper discussions were needed. "The matter is not settled and done," officials said, adding that if an automated system caused the error, Meta must improve its tools.

"The Prime Minister of the world's largest democracy uploads his first direct selfie video to connect with India's youth... and Facebook restricts it???"

— Priti Gandhi, BJP leader, on X

Broader Regulatory Pressure

The video incident comes amid an intensifying pattern of regulatory friction between New Delhi and Meta. In recent weeks, the government issued a notice to WhatsApp over a proposed username feature, flagging concerns that it could fuel fraud and impersonation attacks. WhatsApp agreed not to launch the feature in India until discussions are complete.

MeitY also ordered Instagram to disable all advertisements promoting child sexual exploitation material, demanding a detailed explanation. And Meta's since-scrapped Muse Image AI generator drew government scrutiny over data privacy and consent before the company pulled the feature globally.

India tightened its content rules earlier this year, requiring platforms to remove unlawful content flagged by courts or the government within three hours — down from 36 — or lose their legal shield from liability for user-generated content.

Police Case Against Meta India Head

In a separate but related development, Hyderabad police registered a case against Meta India managing director Arun Srinivas over multiple Facebook videos depicting Modi in what officers described as an "abusive manner," according to Reuters. Srinivas has led Meta's India operations since July 2025.

India is Facebook's largest market by users. The case is among several filed by supporters of Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party who allege that manipulated videos and images of the prime minister have circulated on Meta-owned platforms during the student protest movement.

What's Next

The government's demand for Meta to explain the video removal "at the highest level" signals that New Delhi intends to hold global tech platforms to stricter standards of accountability. With India's new content-removal timelines already in effect and enforcement actions accelerating, Meta faces a regulatory environment that is growing less forgiving by the month. The company's response — and whether it satisfies Indian officials — could set the tone for how other Silicon Valley firms navigate the country's tightening digital governance framework.
nri_angle: The escalating regulatory battle between India and global tech platforms affects the diaspora's primary channels for staying connected with news and events in India.
